text:
morgan: Hey team — seeing a sharp 429 spike for /v1/generate in prod-us-west over the last 10m. Chart: https://console.redwood.ai/d/alerts/429-spike (hover shows 12% 429s, baseline ~0.4%).

kai: Ugh. Do we know if it's concentrated to a single org or widespread?

morgan: Seems org_id=acme-inc and a couple smaller orgs. Top org shows ~6k requests and 720 429s in 10m.

sandeep: Proposed alerting thresholds: P1 if 429_rate > 5% AND total_requests > 500 in 5m; P2 if 2-5% and >200 requests. Also add an absolute-count guard: >1000 429s in 10m => page.

anya: For CS playbook: we should have a templated note and recommended mitigation steps (reduce parallelism, backoff, request quota increase link). I'll draft. :memo:

alerts-bot: ALARM: 429-rate-high (prod-us-west) — 12% 429s over 10m (triggered at 5% threshold).

cs-bot: Notifying CS on-call: @oncall-cs.

kai: Dashboard panels to add: per-org 429_rate, per-key 429_count, top 10 endpoints by 429, token-bucket fill per org, last successful -> last-error latency. Also show model fallback counts.

morgan: Runbook (quick checklist for SRE):
1) Identify top orgs: run SQL / telemetry query
```
SELECT org_id, count(*) as total, sum(CASE WHEN status=429 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as errors
FROM http_requests
WHERE ts > NOW() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY org_id
ORDER BY errors DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
2) Check rate-limiter logs: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=rate-limiter --tail=500 | grep 429`
3) Check quota service for token bucket state (example k/v store): `redis-cli HGETALL quota:org:1234`
4) Verify we returned `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers to callers.
5) If system-wide, check autoscaler & dedicated pool pressure (gpu_util, queue_depth).

sandeep: If it's single-org saturation: temporary mitigations:
- decrease that org's burst allowance (scale down bucket) OR
- apply short-term hard throttle via routing policy to keep platform healthy
- enable model fallback to smaller model with transparent routing (if policy allows)

anya: CS message template (short):
"Hi — we're seeing your app exceed configured request quotas which caused rate-limited responses (429). Recommended: reduce parallel requests, add exponential backoff, or request a quota increase in Console: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/<org_id>/quotas. If you want, we can temporarily raise your burst for 1 hour while you rollout fixes."

kai: Alerting implementation notes:
- metric: `sum(rate(http_requests{status=~"4.."}[5m])) by (org_id,status)` + filter status=429
- firing if `errors/total_requests > 0.05` and `total_requests > 500`
- include annotation with top 5 orgs and link to dashboard
- add runbook link + pager escalation (page if >1000 429s in 10m)

morgan: Telemetry queries for runbook (prometheus-ish):
```
100 * sum(increase(http_requests_total{status="429"}[10m])) by (org_id)
/ sum(increase(http_requests_total[10m]))
```
Then sort by the result and surface top offenders.

anya: Also put a small panel on the console home for any org exceeding 3% 429s in last 30m so CS can proactively reach out.

alerts-bot: NOTE: make sure alerts include `impact:per-org` label so we can route to CS.

morgan: Implementation plan: I'll add the alert rule and the dashboard panels, sandeep will add the short SRE runbook steps in PagerDuty runbook, anya will draft CS templates and notification rules.

sandeep: For long-term: we should consider per-org adaptive burst sizing based on historical QPS and a quota smoothing window (leaky-bucket vs token-bucket tuning). Add to roadmap.

kai: small UX ask: Console quota page should show recent 429 spikes and a one-click 'request quick burst' that triggers a temporary burst increase with an audit log. That will cut down CS coordination.

anya: Agree. I'll add to the feature backlog and include CS flow.

morgan: OK i'm going to push the alert changes now. Paging @oncall-sre if it fires again. :phone: 

cs-bot: Template drafted and saved at https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/cs/playbooks/429-quota.md

morgan: Thanks — will follow up in this thread with the new alert rule id and dashboard link. :thumbsup:
